title: com.apple.mDNSResponder on macos: compound failure — missing_dependency + resource_limit
scenario: A production com.apple.mDNSResponder (dns) on macos will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: a required unit/socket is not started AND a systemd/ulimit resource cap kills the service (OOM/nofile). the dependency restart storms hit a resource cap, so both must be raised and ordered. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'missing_dependency' and 'resource_limit' on com.apple.mDNSResponder
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `com.apple.mDNSResponder` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `log show --predicate 'process == "com.apple.mDNSResponder"' --last 30m` shows TWO distinct signals ('dependency job failed' and 'Killed / too many open files').
Interaction: the dependency restart storms hit a resource cap, so both must be raised and ordered.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'missing_dependency': inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit.
Then address 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `com.apple.mDNSResponder` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 53 if applicable) with BOTH 'missing_dependency' and 'resource_limit' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Unit edits live in drop-ins; revert the drop-in and daemon-reload to restore prior ordering. Limit overrides are drop-in files; revert to restore defaults. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: the dependency restart storms hit a resource cap, so both must be raised and ordered

possible_mistakes: restart the visible service repeatedly, ignoring the upstream failure
raise the wrong limit (nofile when it was memory)
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: the dependency restart storms hit a resource cap, so both must be raised and ordered.
reference_solution: Resolve 'missing_dependency' first: inspect the failed dependency in the logs; repair/start the upstream unit
Then resolve 'resource_limit': identify which limit was hit from the logs; raise it in the unit override or limits.conf
Validate after each step: dscacheutil -q host -a name localhost
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio com.apple.mDNSResponder non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (missing_dependency e resource_limit). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
